You are doing functional research for "Atlas ERP", an open-source ERP whose explicit benchmark is SAP S/4HANA. Your assigned S/4HANA area: Fiori UX & Embedded Analytics.

TASK: Establish what this area actually covers in current S/4HANA (2025/2026), identify the 6-12 capabilities practitioners consider essential, and judge each against the planned Atlas v1 scope below.

METHOD: Use WebSearch (and WebFetch for promising pages) - 2 to 5 targeted searches. Prefer SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, and reputable ERP consulting sources. If web tools are unavailable or consistently fail, fall back to your embedded knowledge of S/4HANA and say so explicitly in the overview field.

COVER AT MINIMUM: Fiori design system and role-based launchpad (tiles, KPIs, spaces/pages), key Fiori app types (list report, object page, overview page), embedded analytics (CDS views, analytical queries, KPI tiles), and what makes the S/4HANA UX distinctive.

PLANNED ATLAS V1 SCOPE FOR THIS AREA (judge full/partial/out-of-scope against THIS, not your own ideas):
Fiori-inspired role-based home pages: each role sees tiles for its apps and KPIs; in-house component library (data grid, form builder, kanban, dashboard cards, document-flow viewer); role-based dashboards (cash position, AR/AP aging, inventory value, open orders, OTD%, WIP); generic report builder (entity + columns + filters + group-by -> JSON grid + CSV export).

RULES:
- atlas_v1 = "full" when Atlas v1 plans the practitioner-essential core of the capability; "partial" when a meaningful but reduced subset is planned; "out-of-scope" when none of it is planned.
- Every "partial" and "out-of-scope" entry MUST have a non-empty reason (why cut / where the boundary sits) and later_path (how to add it later in one line).
- atlas_module must be one of: finance, inventory, procurement, sales, manufacturing, quality, maintenance, hr, projects, crm, reporting, admin, industry, core, frontend, or "-" for out-of-scope.
- Be honest: if S/4HANA has an essential capability the Atlas plan misses entirely, include it as out-of-scope rather than omitting it.

Your final output is consumed by a script - return only the structured data.

## Key Findings:

**Spaces and Pages Architecture:**
Spaces are assigned to users based on their Business Roles, and users can be assigned to more than one space. The launchpad is role-based, meaning the user's role determines which app tiles are shown. Spaces and Pages automatically respect authorizations—unauthorized tiles are hidden, and empty sections/pages/spaces are hidden.

Insights Tiles display dynamic content you can use to monitor valuable KPIs at a glance. A tile is a clickable object that opens an app or target, showing a title, subtitle, icon, number, KPI, or status information.

With SAP S/4HANA 2025, the Launchpad Content Aggregator (/UI2/FLPCA) also includes spaces and pages layouts. Improvements with SAP S/4HANA 2025 release make composite role design easier, including the ability to hide empty spaces and empty pages via launchpad configuration parameter.

**Fiori 4.0 Features:**
SAP S/4HANA 2025 introduced Fiori 4.0 with AI-Assisted Enterprise Search, Financial Insights, and the ability to hide empty spaces/pages automatically.

Based on the search results, here's a comprehensive overview of S/4HANA Embedded Analytics, CDS views, analytical queries, and KPI tiles:

## Core Architecture

The Virtual Data Model (VDM) is a layered architecture of predefined CDS views in SAP S/4HANA that structures analytical data. It consists of basic, composite, and consumption views, each serving a different purpose—ranging from raw data access to user-facing analytical queries.

## CDS Views and Analytical Queries

Embedded Analytics are based on a technology called "Core Data Services" or "CDS Views". These are scripted views that allow data from the ERP to be manipulated and formatted. Analytical Queries are consumption views built using CDS annotations that expose data for analysis through SAP tools like Fiori, Analysis for Office, or SAP Analytics Cloud.

## KPI Tiles and Smart Business

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are implemented through CDS-based analytical models and published to the SAP Fiori Launchpad as Smart Business tiles. KPI modeling in Embedded Analytics is accomplished through the SAP Smart Business framework, which enables defining, visualizing, and monitoring KPIs in real time. Business users can create KPIs and drill-downs using the "Manage KPIs and Reports" Fiori app. Each KPI is linked to a CDS view or analytical query that provides the underlying data.

## Overview Pages

The Overview Page is an analytical SAP Fiori app that provides all the information a business user needs in a single page, based on a specific job role. An Overview Page focuses the user on the most important performance indicators (KPIs) and offers navigation options to explore the underlying data.

## Real-time Analytics and Data Access

Virtual data models (VDMs) provide the database for Embedded Analytics apps. Unlike SAP Data Warehouse systems, analytics frameworks in SAP S/4HANA no longer rely on replicated data, but instead access posted information directly in the ERP system using Core Data Services (CDS Views).

Based on the web search results, here's a comprehensive overview of SAP Fiori Elements floorplans:

## SAP Fiori Elements Floorplans

SAP Fiori elements is a framework that comprises the most commonly used floorplan templates and is designed to speed up development by reducing the amount of frontend code needed to build SAP Fiori apps.

### Available Floorplans

The currently available floorplans include:

- **Overview page**: Provides a page filled with cards summarizing a business scenario. The cards can be used as a jumping-off point for accessing further information.
- **List report page**: Provides a page where users can view and interact with a large set of items. These are typically accompanied by an object page, used to view details about an item. This combination is sometimes referred to as an LROP (List Report Object Page) app.
- **Analytical list page**: Provides a page where users can access KPI information and visualizations of data alongside a list.
- **Worklist page**: Provides a page where users can process a list of work items or processes.
- **Object page**: Provides details about a single item.

### Key Features

The overview page (OVP) is a new data-driven SAP Fiori app that provides all the information a user needs to view, filter, and react to data in a one-stop-shop page.

The analytical list page (ALP) offers a unique way to analyze data step by step from different perspectives, to investigate a root cause through drilldown, and to act on transactional content.

The object page floorplan is used to view, edit, and create objects.

### Important Notes

The analytical list page and the overview page are only available as SAP Fiori elements.

## Core UX Features

The 2025 SAP Fiori experience brings together the structured power of enterprise data and modern web application usability through the SAP Fiori 3 design system centered on the Horizon visual theme, My Home enhancements, and deeper integration with SAP Business AI and Joule.

## Joule Enterprise Search and AI Integration

Joule is becoming a consistent presence across SAP Start, SAP Mobile Start, and S/4HANA Cloud, adding a subtle AI layer to the user journey rather than redesigning the interface, allowing users to trigger Joule to retrieve insights, ask for summaries, or receive recommended actions in finance or supply chain scenarios.

AI-assisted enterprise search was in beta testing and is now generally available as a base feature.

## Personalization and Smart Features

AI-assisted smart personalization of My Home for insight cards is now a generally available premium feature. Users can regularly use Joule to create insights cards for specific data overviews, such as blocked sales orders or open orders for top customers, and add them directly to the My Home page in the SAP Fiori launchpad.

## Additional AI-Assisted Capabilities

S/4HANA 2025 brings SAP Business AI directly into Fiori apps through features like AI-assisted Easy Filter, Smart Summarization, and Joule-powered navigation.

## Design Consistency

The Horizon design system provides a scalable, consistent language that works across systems and form factors with the principle of design once, deploy everywhere.

input.prompt: List the main tools and capabilities of S/4HANA Embedded Analytics for end users: e.g., multidimensional reports, Query Browser, Manage KPIs and Reports / Smart Business, analytical Fiori apps, overview pages, analytical list pages, SAP Analytics Cloud embedded edition, Analysis for Office. Summarize what each does.

content.content:
# SAP S/4HANA Embedded Analytics: Main Tools and Capabilities

Based on the article, here are the primary tools for end users:

## **Overview Pages**
"Role-based, context-specific overview of operational business data" presented through visual "cards" containing charts, tables, or lists. They enable navigation directly to detailed views or transactional apps with "insight-to-action" functionality.

## **Multidimensional Reports**
Tools for "performing in-depth, context-based analyses of operational data" across numerous dimensions like organization, time, product, and region. Features include pivot-based visualization, dynamic drill-down capabilities, and interactive filtering.

## **Analytical List Pages**
Apps combining "analysis and operational action within a single interface," allowing users to visualize large data volumes, apply filters, and move into detailed processing without switching systems.

## **Smart Business KPIs**
Tile-based dashboards monitoring "key figures in real time" with threshold limits and target ranges (red/yellow/green). Users can drill down from aggregated indicators to detailed levels and navigate to related applications.

## **Extension Tools**
- **Manage KPIs and Reports**: Administrative app for creating and maintaining KPIs
- **SAP Build**: Low-code platform for extending Fiori applications without programming
- **Custom CDS Views & Analytical Queries**: Tools for flexible data modeling and query creation
- **Custom Fields and Logic**: Extensions for existing data models

All operate within the SAP Fiori environment with real-time reporting capabilities.

input.overview: Findings are based on live web research (SAP Help Portal, SAP Community 2025-release blogs, SAP Fiori design system docs, and consulting sources such as PIKON). In current S/4HANA (2025/2026), this area covers the Fiori design system (Horizon theme, SAPUI5/Fiori elements controls), the role-based launchpad organized into spaces and pages with app/KPI/insight tiles, standard floorplans (list report, object page, overview page, analytical list page, worklist), and embedded analytics built on the CDS virtual data model: analytical queries, Smart Business KPI tiles with thresholds and drill-down, multidimensional reports, and self-service query creation - all running live on transactional data with insight-to-action navigation into transactions. The 2025 release adds Fiori 4.0 touches: AI-assisted enterprise search, Joule integration, smart summarization, and AI-personalized My Home insight cards. Atlas v1 covers the essential core of the role-based home page, role dashboards, and tabular self-service reporting; it plans reduced subsets of the component library, floorplan patterns, semantic layer, KPI framework, and drill-down analytics; and it omits enterprise search, per-user personalization/variants, and AI-assisted UX entirely.

capabilities.capability: Role-based launchpad home with spaces/pages and app/KPI tiles
capabilities.description: Single entry point where business roles determine visible spaces, pages, and tiles, including dynamic tiles showing live KPI numbers

capabilities.capability: Fiori design system and UI component library (Horizon, SAPUI5 controls)
capabilities.description: Consistent, responsive, accessible design language and a large control set (smart tables, forms, charts, cards) reused across all apps
capabilities.reason: Atlas plans a focused in-house kit (data grid, form builder, kanban, dashboard cards, document-flow viewer), not a full design system with theming tokens, accessibility standards, and the breadth of SAPUI5 controls
capabilities.later_path: Grow the kit into a documented design system: theme tokens, a11y audit, and new controls added as app screens demand them

capabilities.capability: List report + object page floorplans (transactional work pattern)
capabilities.description: Metadata/annotation-driven filterable list pages paired with detail/edit object pages, including draft handling and table variants
capabilities.reason: Atlas's data grid and form builder cover hand-built list+detail screens, but there is no metadata-driven floorplan generator, draft persistence, or saved table variants
capabilities.later_path: Add a schema-driven page generator that renders list+detail CRUD pages from entity metadata, then layer in drafts and variants

capabilities.description: Role-specific card-based pages (charts, lists, KPIs) giving a one-stop operational overview with navigation to detail apps

capabilities.capability: Analytical list page and multidimensional reporting
capabilities.description: Hybrid chart+table pages and pivot-style reports with interactive drill-down across dimensions (org, time, product, region)
capabilities.reason: Atlas's report builder yields a flat group-by grid with CSV export; no interactive pivoting, drill-down paths, or combined chart+table analysis UI is planned
capabilities.later_path: Add a pivot/drill-down UI and chart rendering on top of existing report-builder queries

capabilities.capability: CDS virtual data model and analytical queries (live semantic layer)
capabilities.description: Layered, reusable CDS views over live transactional data exposing governed analytical queries with measures, hierarchies, and calculated columns - no data replication
capabilities.reason: Atlas's report builder queries raw entities directly, which preserves the live-on-transactional-data principle, but there is no reusable layered view model, calculated/restricted measures, or hierarchies
capabilities.later_path: Introduce a versioned semantic layer (named reusable views and measures) that the report builder, dashboards, and KPI tiles all consume

capabilities.capability: Smart Business KPI framework (Manage KPIs and Reports)
capabilities.description: Key users define KPIs with thresholds/targets (red/amber/green), publish them as launchpad tiles, and drill down from the KPI to detail
capabilities.reason: Atlas ships a fixed set of KPI tiles and dashboard cards; end-user KPI authoring, threshold/target rules, color states, and publish-to-home are not planned
capabilities.later_path: Add a 'manage KPIs' admin screen where a KPI = saved report query + threshold rules, publishable as a home-page tile

capabilities.capability: Self-service query creation and export (Query Browser, custom analytical queries)
capabilities.description: Business users browse available queries and build tabular reports by choosing entity, columns, filters, and groupings, with export to spreadsheet
Generic semantic-object navigation lets users jump from any KPI, card, or report line straight into the underlying transaction; document flow visualizes linked documents
capabilities.reason: Atlas plans a document-flow viewer component, but no generic deep-link/intent framework wiring dashboard cards and report rows to the owning app screens
capabilities.later_path: Define per-entity URL route conventions (deep links) and wire dashboard cards, KPI tiles, and report rows to them

capabilities.description: Launchpad header search spanning apps and business objects (orders, customers, materials, invoices), AI-assisted as of S/4HANA 2025
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 plans only per-report filters; no global cross-entity search or app finder exists anywhere in the plan
capabilities.later_path: Add a global search endpoint over key entities plus a header omnibox that deep-links into list/detail pages

capabilities.description: Per-user saved filter/layout variants, rearranging home tiles and My Home insight cards, and key-user adaptation of screens without code
capabilities.reason: Atlas v1 home pages, dashboards, and grids are role-defined and static; no per-user variants, tile rearrangement, or screen adaptation is planned
capabilities.later_path: Persist per-user grid/filter variants and home-tile layout as JSON preference records keyed by user and screen

capabilities.capability: Joule and AI-assisted UX (NL navigation, smart summarization, easy filter)
capabilities.description: Embedded AI assistant for natural-language navigation, summaries, AI-built insight cards, and AI-assisted filtering across Fiori apps (Fiori 4.0)
capabilities.reason: Flagship 2025 differentiator but not yet baseline-essential, and largely premium/optional even in S/4HANA; nothing AI-related is in the Atlas v1 plan
capabilities.later_path: Once report-builder and search APIs exist, attach an LLM assistant that translates natural language into report definitions and deep links

content.text: Research complete. Structured output delivered with 12 capabilities for the Fiori UX & Embedded Analytics area, judged against the Atlas v1 scope: 4 full (role-based launchpad with tiles/KPIs, role dashboards, self-service report builder), 6 partial (component library, list/object floorplans, multidimensional reporting, CDS semantic layer, Smart Business KPI authoring, insight-to-action navigation), and 3 out-of-scope (enterprise search, per-user personalization/variants, Joule AI UX), based on live web research from SAP Community 2025-release posts, SAP Help Portal, the Fiori design system docs, and consulting sources.
